authors: Julia Francesca Gilbert, Julia Eylül Aysu, István Tóth, Anna Szilasi, Míra Mándoki

mcqs.q: Per this review, the core role of the forensic veterinarian in cruelty cases is to:
mcqs.e: The review frames the forensic veterinarian's central function as objective, legally defensible documentation of findings.

mcqs.q: Which capability does forensic necropsy provide according to the article?
mcqs.e: The review highlights differentiating ante- from post-mortem injury, estimating time of death, and interpreting trauma patterns.

mcqs.q: The recurring system gaps the review identifies are:
o: Standardized training and interdisciplinary collaboration/chain of custody
mcqs.e: It calls for standardized training, interdisciplinary collaboration, and greater legal recognition as the field's main needs.

authors: Francesca Bellini, Alberto Cal, Alessia Liverini, Gianna Regoli, Giancarlo Ruffo

mcqs.q: Animal hoarding is clinically classified as:
o: A manifestation of DSM-5 Hoarding Disorder
mcqs.e: The article recognizes hoarding as a manifestation of Hoarding Disorder per DSM-5 criteria.

mcqs.q: Beyond animal removal, the proposed framework emphasizes:
mcqs.e: High recidivism means longitudinal monitoring and mental-health intervention are essential, not just removing animals.

mcqs.q: The four sequential phases of the operational protocol are:
mcqs.e: The protocol is structured across reporting, on-site inspection, case management, and monitoring.

authors: Nicolás Aradilla, Javier María De Pablo-Moreno, Néstor Porras, Blanca Chinchilla, Antonio Rodríguez-Bertos

mcqs.q: Among the abused cats dying of non-natural causes, the leading cause was:
mcqs.e: Blunt force trauma accounted for 32% of cases, exceeding poisoning (15%) and projectile injury (11%).

mcqs.q: The correlation between the suspected manner of abuse and the final forensic diagnosis was:
mcqs.e: The study reported a very low correlation between presumed abuse type and confirmed diagnosis.

mcqs.q: The low correlation supports which exam takeaway?
o: Field impressions reliably predict cause of death
Objective necropsy/toxicology is required to establish cause and manner
mcqs.e: Presumptive field impressions are unreliable, so objective necropsy and toxicology are needed.

mcqs.q: The two most frequent causes of non-natural death in this Dutch forensic series were:
mcqs.e: Blunt force trauma (30%) and neglect/deprivation (26%) dominated non-natural deaths.

mcqs.q: Legal outcomes for the cases that reached court were generally:
o: Minor penalties such as fines or community service
mcqs.e: Most outcomes were minor penalties, with only one case exceeding six months' imprisonment.

mcqs.q: The most commonly examined species were:
mcqs.e: Companion species predominated: dogs (41.8%) and cats (28.5%).

authors: Sylvia M. Lesnikowski, Sharon Pailler, Emily G. Patterson-Kane

mcqs.q: The structured refeeding protocol for emaciated cruelty-case dogs resulted in:
o: Safe weight gain with no nutrition-related deaths
mcqs.e: No dogs died of nutrition-related issues and the protocol produced successful weight gain.

mcqs.q: Which laboratory findings predicted slower recovery?
mcqs.e: Markers of inflammation/infection—hyperglobulinemia plus neutrophilia or monocytosis—predicted delayed weight gain.

mcqs.q: The forensic significance of documented weight gain on a controlled diet is that it:
o: Indicates prior weight loss was from withheld food (neglect), not disease
mcqs.e: Recovery on adequate feeding is strong evidence the emaciation resulted from food deprivation.

authors: Daniela Averaimo, Alessandra Scagliarini, Pietro Badagliacca, Stefania Salucci, Lucio Marino, Massimiliano Paoletti, Antonio Cocco, Elga E. Tieri, Maria Chiara Cantelmi, Sabrina V. P. Defourny, Angelo Peli, Antonio Petrini

mcqs.q: In this Italian archive, the leading forensic cause of death in pets was:
mcqs.e: Injury was the most frequent cause in pets, versus attack in livestock and unlawful killing in wildlife.

mcqs.q: For wildlife, the leading forensic cause was:
mcqs.e: Unlawful killing was the dominant cause among wildlife cases.

mcqs.q: A key gap the study highlights is:
o: Absence of standardized forensic case-classification (e.g., ICD-11-style coding)
mcqs.e: Definitive classification guidelines are lacking; ICD-11-style coding aids forensic surveillance.

authors: A. Y. Kim, M. Kang, H. Choi, M. Park, J. S. Baek, B. Ku, K. Lee

mcqs.q: The histopathologic hallmark confirming this toxicosis was:
o: Renal tubular necrosis with calcium oxalate crystals
mcqs.e: Acute tubular necrosis with intraluminal calcium oxalate crystals is the signature of ethylene glycol toxicosis.

mcqs.q: The incidental feline parvovirus/coronavirus positivity was interpreted as:
o: Not the proximate cause of death
The cause of the renal lesions
mcqs.e: These infections were judged incidental, not the proximate cause—antifreeze poisoning was.

mcqs.q: Ethylene glycol exposure in the gastric tissue was confirmed by:
o: GC-MS detection of ethylene glycol and glycolic acid
mcqs.e: Validated GC-MS demonstrated ethylene glycol and its metabolite glycolic acid in gastric tissue.

authors: Karelma Frontera-Acevedo, Alanis Boodram, Xaria Luke, Emily Phillip, Rod Suepaul, Lana Gyan

mcqs.q: Approximately what proportion of suspected-abuse cases reached a confirmed cause of death/manner of injury?
mcqs.e: Only 24 of 113 cases (20%) had a confirmed COD/MOI, most commonly trauma.

mcqs.q: The most frequently submitted species was:
mcqs.e: Dogs accounted for 77% of submissions.

mcqs.q: The major barrier to confirming poisoning and prosecuting cases was:
o: Lack of an animal toxicology laboratory
mcqs.e: Absence of a toxicology lab capable of handling animal samples limited confirmation and prosecution.

authors: Yuko Kihara, Yohsuke Makino, Suguru Torimitsu, Fumiko Chiba, Hirotaro Iwase, Makoto Nakajima, Aki Tanaka

mcqs.q: In all three murder-suicide cases, the pets died:
o: By the same cause/mechanism as the human victims
mcqs.e: Human and animal victims died from the same cause, suggesting perpetrators used identical methods.

mcqs.q: These cases provide concrete evidence for:
o: The Link between animal cruelty and interpersonal/family violence
mcqs.e: Pets as co-victims in extreme domestic violence supports The Link concept.

mcqs.q: A practical implication the authors support is:
o: Cross-reporting between human and animal welfare agencies
mcqs.e: Interdisciplinary collaboration and cross-reporting help protect vulnerable humans and animals.

authors: Ineke R. van Herwijnen, Daphne G. L. van Helvoort, Anton H. A. Beijer

mcqs.q: Animal abuse by condition falsification is the veterinary analog of:
o: Munchausen syndrome by proxy (factitious disorder by proxy)
mcqs.e: The caretaker feigns/induces a condition to gain attention or sympathy—analogous to factitious disorder by proxy.

mcqs.q: The dog's recurrent seizures were caused by:
mcqs.e: Post-mortem examination revealed citalopram poisoning as the cause of the seizures.

mcqs.q: The red flags that prompted suspicion were:
o: Early onset plus a household history of prior dogs with seizures
mcqs.e: Atypically early onset and previous household dogs with seizures flagged factitious abuse.

authors: Fabio Pesce, E. Sannino, E. Ragosta, L. Marigliano, G. Picazio, M. Esposito, M. Dimatteo, B. Degli Uberti, S. De Luca, N. Di Caprio, D. Citarella, R. Pinto, G. Fusco, E. De Carlo, G. Miletti

mcqs.q: In forensic medicine, 'overkilling' refers to:
o: Injury far exceeding what is necessary to cause death
mcqs.e: Overkilling denotes unusually massive injuries beyond those needed to kill the victim.

mcqs.q: The two concurrent lethal mechanisms identified in this dog were:
mcqs.e: Lesions of strangulation were confirmed alongside toxicologically proven poisoning.

mcqs.q: The combination that revealed both mechanisms was:
o: Combined radiography, autopsy, histology, and toxicology
mcqs.e: Full-body radiography, autopsy, histology, and toxicology together uncovered concurrent lethal mechanisms.

authors: Giulio Mannocchi, Filippo Roberto Busardò, Luigi Tonino Marsella, Roberta Tittarelli

mcqs.q: Which interpretive limitations does this review identify as complicating veterinary forensic toxicology?
o: Post-mortem changes, species-specific toxicokinetics, and lack of harmonized interpretative criteria
An overabundance of standardized interpretative criteria
Excessive toxicokinetic databases across all species
A complete absence of analytical instrumentation
mcqs.e: The review critically examines post-mortem changes, species-specific toxicokinetics, and the lack of harmonized interpretative criteria as major limitations.

mcqs.q: The analytical mainstay of modern forensic toxicology described is:
mcqs.e: Mass spectrometry-based techniques are emphasized as pivotal forensic tools.

mcqs.q: Malicious poisoning is framed within the review as:
o: Both a cruelty crime and a public/environmental health hazard (One Health)
mcqs.e: The review situates poisoning at the intersection of animal welfare, environmental conservation, and public health.
